keyVerseText: And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee;
rootMeaning: The root of אֲחִיסָמָךְ (ʼĂchîyçâmâk) combines אָח (ʼâch), meaning 'brother,' with סָמַךְ (samak), meaning 'to support.' Thus, the name literally conveys the idea of 'my brother is support' or 'brother of support.' This etymology emphasizes a relational and dependable quality, suggesting someone who embodies the strength and reliability of a supportive brotherly figure, which adds depth beyond a mere proper name to a concept of familial encouragement and steadfastness.
usageInScripture: The word אֲחִיסָמָךְ occurs three times in Scripture, consistently translated as 'of Ahisamach,' referring to an individual rather than a common noun. This consistent usage as a proper name, specifically identifying the father of Oholiab, a skilled artisan from the tribe of Dan, highlights the personal identity and heritage associated with the name. The narrow range of translation underscores its role as a distinct personal figure linked to the sacred task of tabernacle construction.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲחִיסָמָךְ as 'my brother is support' enriches our appreciation of God's provision through faithful individuals in His redemptive plan. Ahisamach, as the father of a gifted craftsman, symbolizes the supportive community God raises up to accomplish His purposes, particularly in worship and tabernacle service. This reflects the biblical truth that God equips His people with wisdom and skill, often through relational and familial bonds, to build His holy dwelling. Recognizing the meaning behind the name invites believers to see their own roles as supportive members within the body of Christ, called to uphold and strengthen one another in service to God.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 31:6 states, 'And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan...' Here, the name Ahisamach identifies the lineage of Oholiab, linking the craftsman's divine gifting to his heritage. The meaning 'my brother is support' subtly underscores the theme of God providing not only gifted individuals but also a supportive community to fulfill His commands. This verse highlights God's intentional empowerment of skilled workers through relational ties, reinforcing the idea that His work is accomplished in the context of faithful fellowship and mutual support.
